papers.name: Component 1 Changing Physical and Human Landscapes

topics.name: Theme 1 Landscapes and Physical Processes
points: 1.1 Distribution of UK landscape types and their geology; factors that make landscapes distinctive
1.1 Human impacts on distinctive UK landscapes (including visitor pressure) and management strategies
1.2 Fluvial processes and landforms in a distinctive UK landscape
1.2 Coastal processes and landforms in a distinctive UK landscape
1.2 Factors affecting rates of landscape change (geology, climate, human activity); contrasting located studies
1.3 Drainage basins of the UK: water stores and flows
1.3 Causes and effects of river flooding, flood hydrographs and a located UK flood study
1.3 Flood management: hard and soft engineering and land-use zoning

topics.name: Theme 2 Rural-urban Links
points: 2.1 The urban-rural continuum in the UK: urban and rural links and counter-urbanisation
2.1 Rural service change, depopulation and sustainable rural communities
2.2 Causes and consequences of population change in the UK
2.2 Challenges for UK towns and cities: brownfield and greenfield development case studies
2.2 Changes in retailing in the UK
2.3 Global patterns of urbanisation
2.3 Urban issues in two contrasting global cities (one LIC or NIC, one HIC)
2.3 How global cities are connected

topics.name: Theme 3 Tectonic Landscapes and Hazards (option)
points: 3.1 Global distribution of tectonic activity
3.1 Plate tectonic processes at plate margins
3.1 Volcanic landforms
3.2 Impacts of tectonic hazards and factors affecting vulnerability
3.2 Reducing risk from tectonic hazards; located volcanic and earthquake events

topics.name: Theme 4 Coastal Hazards and their Management (option)
points: 4.1 Physical factors that make coastlines vulnerable to erosion and flooding
4.1 Human factors that increase coastal vulnerability
4.2 Managing coastal hazards: hard and soft engineering
4.2 Hold the line versus managed retreat; cost-benefit analysis and Shoreline Management Plans
4.2 Impacts of sea-level rise on coastlines

topics.name: Theme 5 Weather, Climate and Ecosystems
points: 5.1 Evidence for climate change during the Quaternary period
5.1 Causes of climate change: the carbon cycle and the greenhouse effect
5.2 Global atmospheric circulation
5.2 Low-pressure and high-pressure weather hazards: located studies and responses
5.2 UK weather and climate and its variations
5.3 Global biomes: tropical rainforest and one contrasting biome
5.3 Ecosystem processes and biodiversity; a located small-scale UK ecosystem
5.4 Human use of ecosystems and the impacts of energy production
5.4 Human modification of ecosystems and sustainable management

topics.name: Theme 6 Development and Resource Issues
points: 6.1 Measuring development (e.g. GNI and GDP) and its limitations; the development gap
6.2 Causes of uneven development at the global scale: geo-political trade, MNCs and tourism
6.2 Consequences of uneven development within one LIC and one NIC; responses such as aid and fair trade
6.3 Changing water demand, water footprints and water security
6.3 Water management at international and small scales; groundwater over-abstraction
6.4 Regional inequality in one LIC or NIC
6.4 The UK north-south divide and policies to reduce regional inequality

topics.name: Theme 7 Social Development (option)
points: 7.1 Measuring social development: gender and health measures
7.1 The social development gap
7.2 Birth and death rates, infant mortality and education
7.2 Refugees and uneven social development
7.2 HIV and malaria in sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia: consequences and responses

topics.name: Theme 8 Environmental Challenges (option)
points: 8.1 Consumerism, ecological footprints and impacts on the environment
8.1 Effects of and responses to climate change
8.2 Management of ecosystems: habitat restoration, including wetlands
8.2 Sustainable tourism and ecosystem management

topics.name: Part A Fieldwork methodologies, representation and analysis
points: Posing enquiry questions and hypotheses
Collecting evidence: sampling, quantitative and qualitative methods and secondary sources
Methodological approaches: transects, change over time, qualitative surveys and geographical flows
Processing and presenting fieldwork data
Analysing patterns and relating them to wider geographical knowledge
Drawing evidenced conclusions
Evaluating limitations: accuracy, reliability and bias

topics.name: Part B Conceptual frameworks in fieldwork
points: Place
Sphere of influence
Cycles and flows
Mitigating risk
Sustainability
Inequality

topics.name: Part C Applying geography to a UK context and decision making
points: Applying geographical concepts and knowledge to an unfamiliar UK issue
Making and justifying a decision between options
Mathematical and statistical techniques (Appendix A)
